question.worked_solution:
For this integral we choose $u=2{x}^{3}$ and $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

| **Derivatives** | **Integrals** | **Sign** | **Same-color Products** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2{x}^{3}$ | $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ |  |  |
| $6{x}^{2}$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}$ | $+$ | $-{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)$ |
| $12x$ | $-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}$ | $-$ | $\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}$ |
| $12$ | $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{8}$ | $+$ | $\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}$ |
| $0$ | $\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{16}$ | $-$ | $-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}$ |

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =-{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C \\  & =(3x-2{x}^{3})\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+(6{x}^{2}-3)\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$
